subject: Evidence access & delegation for partner GRC integrations (terms discussion)
messages:
From: Auditorium Security <security@auditorium-sec.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: PenTestCo <ops@pentestco.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence transport + delegated access model for GRC integration

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Following internally we've sketched an operational approach for sharing SOC2/pen-test artifacts into partner GRCs without broad data exposure. High level ask: define the delegated access model and retention controls so our ops and your platform team can implement automated handoffs.

Key items we want to align on:
- Evidence access matrix (who can read/download vs view-only) — see attached Exhibit A.
- Chain-of-custody: transfer channels (S3 presigned, SFTP, direct API upload), PGP or envelope encryption, and audit trails.
- Retention / deletion triggers tied to agreements or customer requests.
- KMS integration / encryption-at-rest requirements and whether Redwood will hold keys or we use a shared escrow.
- Point of contact for emergency redaction requests and for auditor re-requests.

We're attaching a draft access matrix and a short MOU outline. We expect PenTestCo to operate under a delegated role with limited download rights; they will run scheduled tests and push artifacts to a secure bucket.

Would like to schedule a 30-minute sync this week to resolve the access matrix and agree on the SFTP/API flow. Proposed times: Thu 10:00–11:00 PDT or Fri 09:00–10:00 PDT.

[Attachment: exhibit-A-evidence-access-matrix.xlsx]
[Attachment: mou-outline-draft.pdf]

Thanks,
Asha Patel
Head of Integrations
Auditorium Security
security@auditorium-sec.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence transport + delegated access model for GRC integration

Asha — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments. Vanessa and Karthik are copied from our Partner Ops and Security Integrations teams. Short answers up front: Redwood can support both presigned S3 and direct API ingestion to our Evidence Broker; we support per-artifact ACLs, evented audit logs, and optional customer-managed KMS.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm the access matrix rows where Redwood is "platform owner" vs. "delegated partner" (I've annotated Exhibit A and attached a one-page note).
- Agree the transfer channel for initial onboarding (we prefer direct API for automation; presigned S3 acceptable for short-term).
- Draft a short-term SLA for evidence retention and deletion windows (30/90/365 day options) to be included in the MOU.

Can we take Thu 10:00 PDT for the sync. Vanessa — can you lead the runbook/SLAs? Karthik — pls weigh in on KMS key-holding options and pen-test access constraints.

Onward,
Marcus Lin
Head of Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Asha — appreciate the concrete draft. A few operational notes from Partner Ops/security: 

Operational bullets for the sync: 
- SLA banding: suggest we start with a 90-day retention default, with options for 30/365 where customers request. Include an archival flag for encryption-only retention.
- Access roles: we propose three roles — Viewer (metadata & redacted preview), Auditor (download permitted, watermarking enabled), and Custodian (full download, restricted to named org reps).
- Transfer channels: for initial onboarding we accept S3 presigned uploads. Long term we prefer the API (MDM+callback for ingestion events).
- KMS: Redwood can act as key custodian using HSM-backed KMS, or we can support Customer-managed keys in the customer's cloud account. For regulated customers we'll recommend CMK (customer-managed).
- Chain-of-custody: require signed transfer manifests from PenTestCo and hash verification on ingest; we'll store manifests in a tamper-evident log.

Action items before Thu 10:00 PDT sync: 
1) Asha: confirm whether Auditorium wants Redwood to provide watermarking and whether PenTestCo should have Auditor or Custodian rights.
2) PenTestCo: share a sample transfer manifest and a short snippet of their SFTP/API workflow.
3) Marcus: prepare a one-page SLA table (retention / deletion / emergency redaction response times).

I'll also prepare a short template SLA and a redaction runbook to circulate immediately after our call. Linking a draft DocuSign envelope for the MOU so legal can start review: https://www.docusign.com/link/to/mou-draft

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Manager, Partner Operations
Redwood Inference
